title: Fire safety and evacuation
siteNotes: Where the assembly point is, and the back-up if it is blocked
Where the fire alarm panel is and how to read it
Where the manual call points and fire extinguishers are, and which types are fitted
The venue's evacuation plan, including bedrooms, the restaurant, the bar and the marquee or function room
Who the fire marshals are and who does the roll call
How each department finds out who is on shift, and how guests who need help are recorded
Fire door locations and which doors must never be propped open
Whether the building has a designated evacuation lift for disabled guests. The session's 'never use a lift' rule is for ordinary lifts; any evacuation lift is used only as the evacuation plan says.
legalNotes: Staff must be given suitable fire safety instruction and training, on induction and again when risks change: Regulatory Reform (Fire Safety) Order 2005, art. 21. Index entry; https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2005/1541/article/21

The employer (the responsible person) must carry out a fire risk assessment, keep fire safety measures in place, plan for an emergency, and tell staff about the risks: gov.uk 'Workplace fire safety: your responsibilities' https://www.gov.uk/workplace-fire-safety-your-responsibilities (checked).

Keeping escape routes clear and fire doors shut: general requirement of the 2005 Order (art. 14, emergency routes and exits) and the government hotel risk assessment guide, https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/fire-safety-risk-assessment-sleeping-accommodation . The guide is a 148-page PDF that could not be read in full here; the 'never wedge a fire door' rule is standard practice and is not tied to a specific page.
Do not use lifts in a fire: standard fire service advice. Not checked against a specific page in this session.
Raise the alarm, call 999, evacuate, do not go back for belongings: standard fire service advice. Not checked against a specific page in this session.

Extinguisher use: 'Only if trained and it is safe' is standard guidance. The PASS method (Pull, Aim, Squeeze, Sweep) is widely taught, but the venue's extinguisher types and training must be confirmed by the manager. Not checked against a specific page in this session.

Guests who need help to leave: the responsible person must plan for them (the 2005 Order requires an emergency plan). Personal emergency evacuation plans are a recognised way of doing this; the venue's arrangements are a siteNote.
Fire marshals need a separate practical course (see index.json).

Review Oct 2026: art. 21 wording re-read on legislation.gov.uk (adequate safety training on being employed, when exposed to new or increased risks, repeated periodically, in working hours). Employees' own duties to take care and co-operate are in art. 23. No change needed to slides.

Review Oct 2026: 'never use a lift' is standard fire service advice for ordinary lifts; purpose-built evacuation lifts are the exception and are a siteNote. 'Check toilets and storerooms if it is safe' is good practice, not a legal requirement, and is worded as conditional. Unchanged.

cards.title: Fire safety and evacuation
cards.body:
By the end of this session you can:
- act straight away if you find a fire
- help guests and colleagues get out
- keep escape routes clear every shift

cards.title: Guests rely on you
cards.body:
In a hotel, guests may be asleep, unfamiliar with the building, or have had a drink. They will look to staff. The business has a legal duty to train you, and you have a part to play in keeping everyone safe.

> Your manager will show you the evacuation plan for each part of the building.

items.title: Bedrooms
items.text: Guests may be asleep and slow to react.

items.title: Restaurant and bar
items.text: Busy, noisy, and full of people who do not know the exits.

items.title: Weddings and events
items.text: Large groups, music and unfamiliar rooms.

cards.title: If you find a fire
cards.body: Raise the alarm first. Do not try to deal with it before you have told others. Never put yourself at risk.

items.title: Shout
items.text: Warn people nearby and get them out.
Call the fire service. Say where the fire is.

items.title: Leave
items.text: Close doors behind you and go to the assembly point.

cards.title: Fight a fire only if it is safe
cards.body:
Using an extinguisher is a choice, not a duty. Only try if you have been trained, the fire is small, you have a clear way out behind you, and the alarm has been raised.

> Your manager will show you where the extinguishers are and which type is which.

right.title: Walk away if
items: Your exit could be cut off

cards.title: Getting everyone out
cards.body:
Assume every alarm is real. Leave by the nearest safe exit and help guests do the same. Do not stop to collect belongings or finish a task.

- Calmly direct guests and say 'please leave now'
- Check toilets and storerooms on your way if it is safe
- Never use a lift

cards.title: Helping people who cannot leave alone
cards.body:
Some guests may have a disability, be unwell, or have young children. They need help to leave, not a lift. Tell the fire service where anyone is left behind and never leave them without telling someone.

> Your manager will show you how guests who need help are recorded and who assists them.

items.title: Tell the fire service
items.text: Say where anyone is still inside.

items.title: Stay with them if safe
items.text: Or wait in a safe place until help comes.

cards.title: Keep escape routes clear
cards.body:
Fire doors slow smoke and flames. A wedged door does nothing. Corridors, stairs and exits must stay clear, so don't leave trolleys, linen, boxes or chairs in them, even for a minute.

- Report anything blocked or damaged straight away

right.title: Never
items: Park a trolley in a corridor

cards.title: Assembly point and roll call
cards.body:
Go straight to the assembly point and stay there. Do not wander back in. Tell your manager or fire marshal who you have seen, or who is missing. Only the fire service can say when it is safe to go back in.

> Your manager will show you where the assembly point is.

items.title: Go to the point
items.text: Take the route away from the fire.

items.title: Report
items.text: Tell the marshal who is missing.

cards.title: Remember
cards.body:
- Raise the alarm first, then 999
- Fight a fire only if trained, safe and with a clear exit
- Never use a lift; leave belongings behind
- Keep escape routes clear and never wedge fire doors open
- Go to the assembly point and report who is missing

cards.q: You find smoke coming from a storeroom. What do you do first?
options: Open the door to see how bad it is
Find a manager to ask what to do
Fetch an extinguisher
Raise the alarm and warn people nearby
cards.why: Raise the alarm first so everyone starts getting out. Then call 999. Do not open the door or fight the fire before others are warned.

cards.q: A fire door is heavy, so it is fine to wedge it open during a busy service if you take the wedge out afterwards.
cards.why: A fire door only works when closed. A wedge defeats it. Report the door if it is hard to use.

cards.q: The alarm goes off while you are in the restaurant and a guest wants to go back for their coat. What do you say?
options: Leave it, please leave now and go to the assembly point
Go quickly, but come straight back to us
Wait here until the alarm has stopped ringing
Take the lift, as it is quicker than the stairs
cards.why: Nobody goes back for belongings, and lifts are never used in a fire. Direct people calmly to the nearest safe exit.

cards.q: Which TWO must be true before you try to put out a small fire with an extinguisher?
options: You have been trained to use it
The fire is between you and the exit
You have a clear way out behind you
You have not yet raised the alarm
A guest has asked you to
cards.why: Only fight a fire if you are trained, it is safe, the alarm is raised and you can leave behind you.

cards.q: At the assembly point you notice a colleague who was on the second floor is not there. What do you do?
options: Go back inside to look for them yourself
Assume they left early and went home
Tell the fire marshal or your manager straight away
Wait until everyone has gone to ask around
cards.why: Report who is missing at once. The fire service decides when and how to search. Do not re-enter the building.

cards.q: The alarm is sounding and a lift is right beside you, so taking it is the quickest way to get a guest down.
cards.why: Never use a lift in a fire. Use the stairs or the nearest safe exit.

cards.q: A guest in a room says they cannot manage the stairs on their own while the alarm sounds. What do you do?
options: Tell them to wait until the alarm stops
Tell the fire service where they are and stay if safe
Carry them down the stairs yourself, on your own
Say they should use the lift as it is quicker
cards.why: People who cannot leave alone must be reported to the fire service, and you stay with them only if it is safe.

cards.q: You are clearing glasses and find a linen trolley parked in the corridor outside a fire exit. What do you do?
options: Leave it there, as housekeeping will be back soon
Push it into a corner of the corridor out of the way
Move it clear and tell your manager it blocked the exit
Put a sign on it so people know to avoid it
cards.why: Escape routes must stay clear at all times, even for a minute.

cards.q: If you have been given an extinguisher and the fire is small, you must always try to put it out.
cards.why: Fighting a fire is a choice. Only try if trained and safe; otherwise raise the alarm and leave.

cards.q: The fire service arrives while you are at the assembly point. A colleague wants to fetch their phone from the staff room. What do you say?
options: Go ahead, as it will only take a minute
Only fire marshals are allowed to go back in
Wait ten minutes and then go in for it
No, stay out until the fire service says it is safe
cards.why: Nobody goes back in until the fire service says it is safe.
